'''Bob Brooks''' (born {{birth based on age as of date|53|2026|8|12|noage=1}}) is an American politician, labor leader and retired firefighter. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], he is the representative-elect for [[Pennsylvania's 7th congressional district]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Pennsylvania#District 7|2026]].

==Early life and firefighting==
Brooks was born in [[North Adams, Massachusetts]], and raised by his mother.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2026/08/12/four-pennsylvania-districts-could-flip-house-2026-midterms/|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|title=Inside four Pennsylvania races that could flip the House|date=August 12, 2026|author=Zito, Salena}}</ref><ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|url=https://time.com/7379790/democratic-party-blue-collar-candidates/|website=[[Time.com]]|title=The Democrats’ Blue-Collar Brigade|author=Terruso, Julia|date=February 23, 2026}}</ref> He worked as a [[paperboy]] at age 10 and later at a factory while attending high school.<ref name="auto"/> In high school, he played [[American football|football]].<ref name="auto4"/> Shortly prior to his final football game, his house burned down.<ref name="auto4"/> Afterwards, he and his mother moved to [[Bath, Pennsylvania]], in 1992.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ppffa.org/index_blank.cfm?zone=/unionactive/officers.cfm|publisher=Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association|access-date=August 18, 2026|title=Officers & Staff}}</ref> Brooks attended college for a time before dropping out.<ref name="auto"/> He worked various jobs in the subsequent years, including as a bartender, truck driver, gas station attendant, cook, and dishwasher.<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jun/08/bob-brooks-pennsylvania-congress|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|title=‘I’m tired of getting kicked in the teeth’: firefighting union leader seeks to shake up Congress|author=Sainato, Michael|date=June 8, 2026}}</ref>

In 2005, Brooks began working as a [[firefighter]] in [[Bethlehem, Pennsylvania]], serving 20 years until his retirement in March 2025.<ref name="auto1"/><ref name="auto3"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lehighvalleypublicmedia.org/news/elections/firefighter-union-boss-bob-brooks-jumps-into-lehigh-valley-congressional-race/|publisher=[[Lehigh Valley Public Media]]|title=Firefighter union boss Bob Brooks jumps into Lehigh Valley congressional race|date=August 26, 2025|author=Shortell, Tom}}</ref> He was also active as a labor leader, serving many positions with the local chapter of the [[International Association of Fire Fighters]], "including roster duty chairman, trustee, vice president, secretary-treasurer, and president."<ref name="auto5">{{Cite web|url=https://internationalfireandsafetyjournal.com/firefighter-bob-brooks-congress-pennsylvania/|website=International Fire & Safety Journal|title=From the firehouse to Congress: Bob Brooks takes his fight to Washington|author=Hoey, Iain|date=September 2, 2025}}</ref> In 2021, he became the president of the Pennsylvania Professional Fire Fighters Association, a union with a membership of 8,000.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/bob-brooks-hakeem-jeffries-josh-shapiro-bethlehem-20260726.html|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|title=Hakeem Jeffries and Josh Shapiro rally for Democrat Bob Brooks, 100 days ahead of a competitive congressional race in Lehigh Valley|date=July 26, 2026|author=Baruchman, Michelle}}</ref> Brooks is also the owner of a snow removal and lawn care business.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/bob-brooks-lehigh-valley-joins-democratic-primary-20250826.html|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|title=A firefighter running for Congress in the Lehigh Valley has backing from Bernie Sanders and Josh Shapiro|date=August 26, 2025|author=Terruso, Julia}}</ref>

Brooks is married and has four children.<ref name="auto5"/> He has served as a high school [[baseball]] coach at [[Nazareth Area High School]].<ref name="auto1"/>

==Political career==
In August 2025, Brooks declared his candidacy for the [[United States House of Representatives]] for [[Pennsylvania's 7th congressional district]] as a member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/26/bob-brooks-firefighter-pa07-dem-launch-00523842|website=[[Politico]]|title=Firefighters union leader launches bid for battleground Pennsylvania House seat|author=Otterbein, Holly|date=August 26, 2025}}</ref> Among those to endorse him were Governor [[Josh Shapiro]] and Vermont Senator [[Bernie Sanders]].<ref name="auto2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/19/us/politics/bob-brooks-pennsylvania-house-primary.html|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|title=Bob Brooks, Labor Leader Backed by Top Democrats, Wins Pennsylvania House Primary|author=Robinson, Taylor; Browning, Kellen|date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> Endorsed by the [[Blue Dog Coalition|Blue Dog PAC]]<ref>https://bluedogdems.com/bob-brooks/</ref>, he won the Democratic primary on May 19, 2026, with 41% of the vote, winning against [[Ryan Crosswell]], Lamont McClure and Carol Obando-Derstine.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/05/19/brooks-wins-pennsylvania-house-primary-00929052|website=[[Politico]]|title=Shapiro-backed Brooks wins competitive Pennsylvania primary|author=Kashinsky, Lisa|date=May 19, 2026}}</ref> In the general election, he succeeded over incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Ryan Mackenzie]] in the key U.S. House race.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6176157-democrat-bob-brooks-wins-pa-district/ |access-date=4 November 2026}}</ref><ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.inquirer.com/politics/pennsylvania/pennsylvania-primary-lehigh-valley-bob-brooks-20260507.html|newspaper=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|title=Will Democratic leaders’ ‘working-class’ candidate in the high-stakes Lehigh Valley race be the answer they’re looking for?|author=Janesch, Sam|date=May 7, 2026}}</ref>
